title: Lessons on Operations and Safe Distancing Measures Gleaned from 14 October 2020 MRT Service Disruption Incident
what_it_is: Lessons on Operations and Safe Distancing Measures Gleaned from 14 October 2020 MRT Service Disruption Incident

sections.label: Questions on 14 October 2020 MRT disruption
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Transport about the 14 October 2020 MRT disruption, which affected over 120,000 commuters, covering preparedness, crowd control, protocols, causes, recovery time and lessons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport in view of the recent MRT breakdown on 14 October 2020 (a) whether there are sufficient business continuity plans and emergency preparedness exercises conducted on a regular basis to ensure that the relevant teams know what to do in the event of a power failure; and (b) how long has it taken for the crowd control process to kick in and what have been the measures implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport when buses or trains are stranded at peak hours (a) what are the protocols in place to ensure safe distancing measures and good ventilation for the commuters; (b) whether public transport workers are trained to guide commuters to safety and address their concerns; and (c) what are the lessons learned from the MRT disruption on 14 October 2020 with regard to crowd management and safe distancing measures and how will this be improved upon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what was the cause of the cable insulation fault which triggered the MRT disruption on 14 October 2020; (b) why did the circuit breaker in the vicinity of Tuas Link and Tuas West Road fail to isolate the cable insulation fault; and (c) why was the cable insulation fault not isolated before SMRT attempted to draw power from the Buona Vista intake station resulting in the power supply disruption to Circle Line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) given its past experience, whether SMRT could have taken much less time to complete passenger recovery or evacuation during the MRT disruption on 14 October 2020; and (b) what were the reasons for the delay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport what are the key lessons arising from the MRT disruption of 14 October 2020 and what measures will be taken to ensure that similar future incidents will be avoided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The 14 October 2020 incident was significant and affected over 120,000 commuters.

sections.label: Cause of disruption
sections.summary: The disruption was caused by concurrent faults and one mistake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The disruption was caused by the occurrence of concurrent faults and one mistake.

sections.label: Alstom power cable replacement
sections.summary: Alstom will conduct a complete replacement of all 150 km of power cables along the Tuas West Extension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Following this recent incident, Alstom will conduct a complete replacement of all the power cables – 150 km of it – along the Tuas West Extension.

sections.label: Trip coil replacement and testing
sections.summary: Alstom will replace all 113 trip coils in circuit breakers along the Tuas West Extension by year end, while SMRT steps up mechanical testing from annually to every six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Alstom will also replace all 113 trip coils in the circuit breakers along the Tuas West Extension by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: During this time, SMRT will also step up the frequency of mechanical testing of the circuit breakers of this sector from annually to every six months.

sections.label: Detrainment and bus bridging response
sections.summary: The Operations Control Centre decided on detrainment 40 minutes in; 6,800 commuters were brought to platforms in under an hour except 78 delayed by weather, with free bus boarding in 10 minutes and 120 bridging buses in 35 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Therefore, as far as possible, the Operations Control Centre will try to restore power to the trains and then bring commuters through the trains to the nearest MRT station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: However, 40 minutes into the disruption, the Operations Control Centre concluded that it could not restore power to the system quickly and, therefore, decided on detrainment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: All 6,800 commuters on the stalled trains were brought safely to the nearest station platform in under an hour, except for the 78 commuters whose detrainment was delayed by inclement weather and lightning risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Free boarding of regular bus services was activated within 10 minutes of the incident to disperse the crowds outside the train stations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: One hundred and twenty bridging buses were in place within 35 minutes of the incident and SMRT staff guided commuters to look for suitable alternative transport arrangements to carry on with their journeys.

sections.label: MRT reliability improvement
sections.summary: The term was coined to remind them of the imperative, improving Mean Kilometres Between Failures from under 200,000 train-km five years ago to more than one million train-km today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We coined the term to remind ourselves of the imperative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This was how we managed to significantly improve the reliability of our MRT system, bringing the Mean Kilometres Between Failures or MKBF from under 200,000 train-km just five years ago to more than one million train-km today.

sections.label: Evening evacuation of three trainloads
sections.summary: That evening, evacuating three trainloads of passengers took half an hour because of the side platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In fact, that evening, it took half an hour to evacuate three trainloads of passengers because of the side platform.

sections.label: Standard operating procedure guideline
sections.summary: The guideline for the specific SOP is typically half an hour, 30 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For specific SOP, typically the guideline is half an hour; 30 minutes.

sections.label: Battery power for light and ventilation
sections.summary: The battery cannot power the aircon but will keep some light and a ventilation fan running for about an hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The battery cannot power the aircon but that there will continue to be a bit of light and some ventilation through a fan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There is a battery that will operate for about an hour.

sections.label: Supplier replaces trip coils and cables
sections.summary: The equipment supplier agreed to replace all 113 trip coils and 150 km of cable wires, and SMRT and LTA staff self-reflected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The equipment supplier came forth, agreed to replace all 113 of trip coils, and 150 km of cable wires and within SMRT and LTA, everyone self-reflected what they could do better.

sections.label: Component life span and faults
sections.summary: The components typically have a life span of 20, 25 or 30 years, so four faults in recent years is premature, which explains Alstom replacing everything.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And they typically have a life span of 20, 25, or 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, this is a bit premature to have four faults in the last few years, which I think explains why Alstom is stepping forward and replacing everything.

sections.label: Doubling frequency and disciplinary action
sections.summary: While components are replaced on this stretch, frequency will be doubled, and wilful wrongdoing will bring disciplinary action, including the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For this stretch, while the components are being replaced, we will step up, double the frequency, so that we make sure it works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If there is gross negligence, in fact, if there is wilful wrongdoing, disciplinary actions will be taken, including even bringing in the Police, if there is wilful wrongdoing.

sections.label: System first commissioned 2018
sections.summary: The system was first commissioned in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Two was when the system was first commissioned; that was 2018.
